# forward_auth

Asks another service whether a request may pass. A 2xx answer allows it; any other answer is given to the client.

| | |
|---|---|
| Runs | before the request is forwarded |
| Default priority | 2100 (higher runs earlier) |
| Attach to | a route, a service, a workspace, or every request (`global`, system workspace only) |
| Switch off everywhere | flag `plugin_forward_auth` set to `false` |

## Configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` (required) | string |  |  |
| `method` | `GET`, `POST`, `HEAD` | `GET` |  |
| `request_headers` | list of object | `["Authorization","Cookie"]` | Request headers sent to the service. |
| `response_headers` | list of object | `[]` | Headers of the service's answer copied onto the forwarded request. |
| `timeout_ms` | integer (≥ 10, ≤ 60000) | `2000` |  |
| `fail_open` | boolean | `false` | When the service cannot be reached: true lets the request through, false refuses it. |
| `cache_secs` | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 3600) | `0` | How long an allowing answer is reused for the same cache_key_headers. 0 asks every time. |
| `cache_key_headers` | list of object | `["Authorization"]` |  |

## When to use it

When the decision belongs to a service you already run: a session store, a permissions service. The gateway asks it for every request and acts on the answer. Any 2xx lets the request through; anything else is returned to the client as it is.

## Examples

Ask an authentication service, and pass the user it names on to the upstream:

```yaml
version: 1
services:
  - name: app
    backends:
      - target: "10.0.0.11:8080"
routes:
  - name: app
    service: app
    paths: [/app]
    plugins:
      - type: forward_auth
        config:
          url: https://auth.example.com/verify
          response_headers: [X-User, X-Roles]
```

Remember an allowing answer for a minute, per session cookie and tenant, and let requests through if the service is down:

```yaml
version: 1
services:
  - name: docs
    backends:
      - target: "10.0.0.12:8080"
routes:
  - name: docs
    service: docs
    paths: [/docs]
    plugins:
      - type: forward_auth
        config:
          url: https://auth.example.com/verify
          request_headers: [Cookie, X-Tenant]
          cache_secs: 60
          cache_key_headers: [Cookie, X-Tenant]
          timeout_ms: 500
          fail_open: true
```

## What the service is sent

A request with the listed `request_headers` of the original, plus `X-Forwarded-Method`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Uri` and `X-Forwarded-For`. The body is not sent.

## What clients see

- The service's own status, headers and body when it refuses.
- `503 AUTH_UNAVAILABLE` when it cannot be reached or does not answer within `timeout_ms`, unless `fail_open` is true.

## Goes well with

`cache_secs` when the service is slower than your traffic allows. Only allowing answers are remembered; choose `cache_key_headers` so that two callers who must be told apart never share an entry.
